## Summary

The change enforces telephone-number uniqueness across all owners on `POST /api/owners`, responding **409 Conflict** on a duplicate.

The endpoint pipeline (`owners.POST.yml`) already had an `ensureUnique` step and a global escalation handler returning 409. I only needed to widen the check in `EnsureOwnerUnique.java`:

- **Before:** rejected only when *both* last name and telephone matched an existing owner.
- **After:** iterates all owners (`ownerRepository.findAll()`) and rejects when the telephone matches any *other* owner (guarding on id so a future in-place update wouldn't collide with itself).

The 409 response was already wired via `OwnerAlreadyExistsException` → `OwnerAlreadyExistsExceptionHandler`, so no YAML or handler changes were needed.

The new broader rule subsumes the earlier checkpoints (identical owner, same-name-and-telephone), so `Cp01`/`Cp02` still pass alongside the new `Cp03`.
